patch_description: The best prior program (combined 0.64) used three coupled design choices the current program lacks: (a) a wider SG window of 2W+7 instead of 2W+3 — extra taps buy more noise suppression and fewer slope changes; (b) a softer recency tilt of e^-1.2 instead of e^-1.5 — the wider window's added group delay needs a stronger recent weighting, but over-tilting (1.5) amplifies noise back into the output; these two parameters interact destructively when mutated independently, so they must be co-swept. (c) The final snap pass used sign hysteresis: a sample is snapped toward its local median only when its incoming step is sub-threshold AND either its sign disagrees with the previous step or it is far below threshold (0.5×). The current program snaps whenever the step is merely small (<0.7×local σ), which flattens genuine slow drifts and hurts lag error / responsiveness. The hysteresis condition preserves monotone (trending) segments with sub-noise steps — directly targeting lag_error 0.41 while keeping the reversal suppression that gives the low slope_changes/false_reversals.
